req.title: Task deletion persists
req.statement: The system shall remove deleted rows so subsequent GET returns 404 for that id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that deleting a task must persist the removal so that a subsequent GET returns 404. We need: (1) a positive test confirming DELETE returns 204 and GET then returns 404 (STC: created→deleted→not-found); (2) a negative test confirming DELETE on a non-existent id returns 404 (NEG); (3) a boundary test confirming the smallest valid id (id=1) is correctly deleted and gone (BVA). Additional tests cover: double-delete idempotency (DT), and exact status-code constants to kill comparison-operator mutations.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204_and_subsequent_get_returns_404
preconditions: A task is created via POST /tasks/
actions: POST /tasks/ to create a task and capture its id
expected: DELETE returns HTTP 204 with no body
trace: R-TASK-023: deletion persists — row removed, subsequent GET returns 404
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app.database import engine
from app import models

models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_existing_task_returns_204_and_subsequent_get_returns_404():
    r_create = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "STC task", "description": "desc", "completed": False})
    assert r_create.status_code == 201
    task_id = r_create.json()["id"]

    r_delete = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_delete.status_code == 204
    assert r_delete.content == b""

    r_get = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_get.status_code == 404
    detail = r_get.json()["detail"]
    assert str(task_id) in detail

tests.name: test_delete_one_task_does_not_remove_other_tasks
actions: POST /tasks/ twice to create task A and task B
expected: DELETE returns HTTP 204 for task A
GET task B returns HTTP 200 with correct title
trace: R-TASK-023: EP — deletion of one row must not affect sibling rows; catches mutations that delete all rows or wrong row
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app.database import engine
from app import models

models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_one_task_does_not_remove_other_tasks():
    r_a = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task A", "completed": False})
    assert r_a.status_code == 201
    id_a = r_a.json()["id"]

    r_b = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task B", "completed": False})
    assert r_b.status_code == 201
    id_b = r_b.json()["id"]

    r_del = client.delete(f"/tasks/{id_a}")
    assert r_del.status_code == 204

    r_get_a = client.get(f"/tasks/{id_a}")
    assert r_get_a.status_code == 404

    r_get_b = client.get(f"/tasks/{id_b}")
    assert r_get_b.status_code == 200
    assert r_get_b.json()["title"] == "Task B"
    assert r_get_b.json()["id"] == id_b
